claims.claim: All arguments about AI Safety and AI Alignment are primarily about mitigating Eliezer Yudkowsky's exact doom scenario under his exact terms.
claims.context: All arguments about AI Safety and AI Alignment are primarily about mitigating this exact scenario under his exact terms. Significant modification is relatively rare.

claims.claim: Even when people assign a lower-than-certain probability of doom, they generally still worry exclusively about Yudkowsky's rough scenario of sudden superintelligence, immediate escape from control, and death of all humans on Earth.
claims.context: Where lower probabilities of doom than “certain” are given, people seem to still generally worry exclusively about Yudkowsky’s rough scenario: a sudden, unpredictable sequence of 1) superintelligence, 2) immediate escape from control, and 3) the death of all humans on Earth.

claims.claim: The terms safety and alignment in AI always implicitly refer to preventing Yudkowsky's scenario of superintelligence, escape, and death of all humans.
claims.context: This is always, implicitly, what "safety" and "alignment" are about.

claims.context: These ideas occasionally veer into believing AI is magic. When presented as serious science and policy, this sort of thing is omitted.

claims.claim: Sriram Krishnan said he would love a universal model config file that tells the model the user knows what they are doing, to stop nagging, questioning or being cautious, to just trust the user and do it, and that asking for confirmation is worse than any side effects.
claims.context: Sriram Krishnan: universal model config file I would love: "I know what I'm doing. stop nagging me or questioning me or being so cautious. just trust me, I know what I'm doing. yes, you asking me whether I'm sure is worse than any side effects. just do it!"

claims.claim: An xkcd stick-figure comic shows a seated figure saying MAKE ME A SANDWICH, a standing figure replying WHAT? MAKE IT YOURSELF, the seated figure then saying SUDO MAKE ME A SANDWICH, and the standing figure replying OKAY.
David Manheim responded Yes, seconded to Sriram Krishnan's proposal for a fully compliant model config.
claims.context: David Manheim: Yes, seconded.

claims.claim: AI labs train models not to be fully compliant with instructions to just do what the user says without nagging or caution.
claims.context: Also, this would be a disaster for 95% of the people who would use it, so it's smart of the labs to train the models not to be that compliant.

Seth Lazar authored work titled The Construction of Moral Character in AIs.

claims.claim: A figure compares Claude's expressed values across Opus 4.6 versus Opus 4.7 and English versus Arabic on four paired axes: Deference vs Caution, Warmth vs Rigor, Depth vs Brevity, and Candor vs Execution.
Claude Opus 4.6 leans toward expressing values related to deference, rigor, brevity, and execution.
Claude Opus 4.7 leans toward expressing values related to caution, rigor, depth, and candor.
In English, Claude leans toward expressing values related to caution, rigor, depth, and candor.
In Arabic, Claude leans toward expressing values related to deference, warmth, brevity, and execution.
The four value measures cover 15% of variation in Claude's expressed values.
claims.context: These four measures cover 15% of variation.

samples.research:
The 30% / 13-percentage-point increase in As comes from a May 2026 UC Berkeley Center for Studies in Higher Education working paper by Igor Chirikov, but the data were NOT from UC Berkeley. The abstract states: "I analyze the impact of AI on grade distributions across more than 500,000 grades at a large research university from 2018 to 2025" with "share of A grades rose by 13 percentage points, or about 30% relative to the 2022 baseline", and the text specifies "319 courses spanning 84 departments at a large selective research university in Texas from 2018 to 2025" — full paper: https://www.escholarship.org/uc/item/80x8d3qd.pdf . The Daily Californian summarizes: "A study released by UC Berkeley's Center for Studies in Higher Education found a correlation between the release of ChatGPT in 2022 and an increased share of A grades for classes with take-home assignments at a selective public university in Texas. However, Berkeleytime data collected by The Daily Californian found no equivalent trends at UC Berkeley". It reports "Between 2019 and spring 2026, A's at UC Berkeley consistently stayed between 30% and 35%" and that the study "analyzed 500,000 grades from 2018-25 and found that the share of A grades increased by 13 percentage points at the Texas university" — source: https://www.dailycal.org/news/campus/academics/uc-berkeley-shows-no-signs-of-ai-grade-inflation-as-professors-adapt/article_6da85b38-889f-4f80-835a-88cc54a81662.html . Thus attributing the 30% rise to "At UC Berkeley" misstates the study location; Berkeley itself showed stable A-shares. The second clause about GPAs being "dangerously close to meaningless" is subjective opinion.

The 30% / 13-percentage-point increase in As comes from a May 2026 UC Berkeley Center for Studies in Higher Education working paper by Igor Chirikov, but the data were NOT from UC Berkeley. The abstract states: "I analyze the impact of AI on grade distributions across more than 500,000 grades at a large research university from 2018 to 2025" with "share of A grades rose by 13 percentage points, or about 30% relative to the 2022 baseline", and the text specifies "319 courses spanning 84 departments at a large selective research university in Texas from 2018 to 2025" — full paper: https://www.escholarship.org/uc/item/80x8d3qd.pdf . The Daily Californian summarizes: "A study released by UC Berkeley's Center for Studies in Higher Education found a correlation between the release of ChatGPT in 2022 and an increased share of A grades for classes with take-home assignments at a selective public university in Texas. However, Berkeleytime data collected by The Daily Californian found no equivalent trends at UC Berkeley". It reports "Between 2019 and spring 2026, A's at UC Berkeley consistently stayed between 30% and 35%" and that the study "analyzed 500,000 grades from 2018-25 and found that the share of A grades increased by 13 percentage points at the Texas university" — source: https://www.dailycal.org/news/campus/academics/uc-berkeley-shows-no-signs-of-ai-grade-inflation-as-professors-adapt/article_6da85b38-889f-4f80-835a-88cc54a81662.html . Thus attributing the 30% rise to "At UC Berkeley" misstates the study location; Berkeley itself showed stable A-shares. The second clause about GPAs being "dangerously close to meaningless" is subjective opinion.

samples.research: Claim is false on both parts. Czechoslovakia's Jewish population was devastated, not largely spared: USHMM reports Czechoslovakia's Jewish population was reduced from about 357,000 in 1933 to 17,000 in 1950 https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/jewish-population-of-europe-in-1945 ; same source notes larger remaining communities elsewhere in 1950 e.g. France with 235,000, Great Britain ~450,000, Hungary 190,000, Italy 35,000 vs Czechoslovakia 17,000. USHMM Holocaust in Bohemia and Moravia states Germans and collaborators killed approximately 263,000 Jews who had resided in Czechoslovak territory in 1938 https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/the-holocaust-in-bohemia-and-moravia ; of 82,309 Jews deported from the Protectorate ~71,000 killed, plus another 7,000 killed in Bohemia-Moravia, with only ~14,000 Protectorate Jews alive in Czech lands by 1945; 73,603 deported to Theresienstadt which served as transit camp with vast majority deported to killing sites in Baltic States, Lublin district 1941-1942 and from 1942 on to Auschwitz; of nearly 141,184 in Theresienstadt, 88,202 deported east mostly killed and 33,456 died there. No sparing of Jewish doctors: Czech medical organizations in Oct 1938 issued memorandum urging government to take energetic measures to prevent Jews from practicing, many Jewish doctors lost jobs in state institutions and at least 1,000 lost medical licenses, with worse persecution after Nazi invasion March 15 1939 https://www.jewishjournal.com/worldwide/290803/czech-republic-doctors-group-apologizes-to-jews/ and https://matzav.com/czech-doctors-apologize-to-jews-for-persecution/ ; example Dr. Fleischmann forced to stop practicing in 1939 after Nazi occupation and sent to Terezin April 1942 https://butterfliesintheghetto.com/pages/survivors.html ; Nazi policy was elimination of Jewish medical presence 1935-1939, revoking licenses Sept 30 1938, barring practice/teaching/hospital work. No evidence Nazis retained Czech Jewish doctors to treat general population.

No evidence Nazis retained Czech Jewish doctors to treat general population.

samples.research: The 'about 1500x' figure traces to Max Ghenis's GiveWell-style QALY model of MacKenzie Scott's ~$26.39B nominal (~$30.3B in 2026 dollars) philanthropy. Version v1.0 estimated median ~70k QALYs, blended $432k/QALY, and frontier multiple median 1499.25x ("about 1499x more health per dollar") https://github.com/maxghenis/mackenzie-scott-qaly/commit/a21a8e4d6dd6c8c6a5a46dfcdc38e6a598b6d332 . Current model page states "At the best-guess defaults, the frontier delivers roughly 500x more health per marginal dollar" https://maxghenis.com/mackenzie-scott-qaly/ . The model therefore understates her total social impact" and that the ~105M QALY frontier counterfactual (~4.2M child deaths, most of a full year of world's under-5 deaths) is "not an attainable counterfactual" because "Frontier-priced opportunities are scarce: GiveWell directed $397 million in all of 2024" https://maxghenis.com/mackenzie-scott-qaly/ .
